title: The Agility Retrofit
role: You are the software architect responsible for making a platform crypto-agile.
objective: Retrofit a crypto boundary across 20 services without breaking production.
environment: Twenty services call a cryptography library directly with algorithm names written in code. Stored hashes and ciphertexts exist in several databases.

hud.label: Cryptographic call sites behind the boundary

state_variables.agility: Cryptographic call sites behind the boundary, starts at 0

choices.text: Audit the call sites and library dependencies to establish a baseline and a metric.
choices.feedback: Correct. You cannot manage what you have not measured; the audit gives you the metric you will track.
Big-bang rewrites of working systems cause outages and hide regressions.

choices.text: Wrap one service and declare victory.
choices.feedback: One wrapped service leaves 19 hard-coded ones and no pattern to follow.

stages.decision_prompt: What does its API look like?

choices.text: A purpose-level API (seal, open, sign, verify) with the algorithm identifier inside the data, selected by policy.
choices.feedback: Correct. Callers never see algorithms, and old data stays readable because the algorithm travels with it.

choices.text: A thin wrapper that still takes algorithm names and key sizes.
choices.feedback: The algorithm leaks into every caller again.

choices.text: Let each team write its own helper functions.
choices.feedback: You get 20 different boundaries and no single place to change an algorithm.

stages.decision_prompt: How do you handle stored data?

choices.text: Version the stored values, keep the old algorithm readable, re-protect in the background, and verify before removing old keys.
choices.feedback: Correct. Stored values are the hard part: the same input now gives a different output, so versions and a verified migration are required.

choices.text: Switch the algorithm and recompute stored hashes.
choices.feedback: Recomputation is impossible for values whose inputs you no longer have, and lookups fail.

choices.text: Leave stored data on the old algorithm forever.
choices.feedback: The old algorithm then remains your real exposure.

stages.decision_prompt: How do you keep it that way?

choices.text: Add a CI rule that forbids direct cryptographic calls outside the boundary, an architecture-review checklist, and a drill that changes an algorithm.
choices.feedback: Correct. Enforcement and practice stop the boundary from rotting.
Documentation without enforcement is ignored under deadline pressure.
New code will bypass the boundary within a few releases.

stages.narrative: The architecture board reviews the retrofit.

bands.title: Agile platform
bands.text: SUCCESS. Most call sites are behind a boundary, production stayed stable, and the next algorithm change is a policy change.

bands.title: Partly agile
bands.text: PARTIAL. Progress is real but incomplete, or it cost stability or time.

bands.title: Retrofit stalled
bands.text: AT RISK. The platform is still hard-coded or became unstable.

resolution.concept_reveal: Retrofit by measuring first, introducing a purpose-level boundary with the algorithm inside the data, migrating stored values with versions and a verified re-protection, and enforcing the boundary in CI. Rewriting everything at once or leaving stored data behind are the two classic failures.

replayability_note: Alternative orders change stability and speed.
